key_insight: Distilling a fixed atomistic foundation model into compact potentials preserves key semiconductor-interface responses while improving simulation speed and accessible system size by several orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Compact distilled potentials enable large-scale simulations of interfacial heat transport and mechanical behavior with responses close to DFT-trained counterparts.
method: Select an EquiformerV3 teacher from 128 pretrained models spanning 22 families, without target-specific fine-tuning.
Train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students on teacher-generated labels.
Compare against DFT-trained students using matched training configurations and architectures.
evidence_signal: Conductance differed by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts in 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces; tensile strength and loading work differed by 2.8% and 1.5% in 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens at 500 K.
watch_item: Committee-based selection improved high-error force fitting but did not consistently improve downstream properties, so label accuracy alone is insufficient validation.
paper_title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
